title: A recording opens in the video editor, for real, in Next
goal: About twenty video features (timeline, split, transitions, speed, punch-in, titles, captions, sound as a layer, video export) are on by default in Next, but all of them live in the editor that next-a-recording-is-a-document opens, and that flag is OFF by default. So a person opening a recording got the old play-and-shorten window and none of the work. Walks set the flag themselves, so nothing caught it. The user found this on 2026-09-23 and was furious: 'I can't create a layer, do transitions, split audio out'.
notes: Root cause found in the intake window: PhotonzApp.swift:161 routes .video to ReleaseExperience.videoEditor when the flag is off. The user's dev app has the flag turned on by hand as of 2026-09-23 04:50.
acceptance: next-a-recording-is-a-document is enabledByDefaultIn [.next], and a person with no stored override opening a recording in Next gets the editor with the timeline

A unit test over FeatureCatalog fails when a flag enabled by default in a release depends on a flag that is off by default in that release; video flags declare that they depend on next-a-recording-is-a-document
A walk opens a recording WITHOUT setting any flag and photographs the timeline, the layers list with the clip in it, and the transport
The old small video window is not what any Next user reaches from opening, dropping or capturing a recording

log.note: Overlaps trim-becomes-a-tool-and-the-recording-window-ret (blocked on the Command S decision). Kept separate on purpose: turning the editor on by default must not wait for the Save question, the user wants to edit video now. Save/trim/window retirement stay in that task.
